content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast cooked on a rotisserie with the skin eaten is a tender source of protein obtained by slowly rotating the meat over heat. This method retains juices, while the skin becomes crispy and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A rotisserie grill allows even cooking thanks to constant rotation of the meat.
Chicken skin contains more fat than the breast itself, but during proper cooking some fat melts, enhancing flavor.
Rotisserie chicken is a tradition popular in the Mediterranean and the Middle East.
Typical rotisserie temperatures range from 180‑200 °C, producing a golden crust.
Boneless chicken breast cooks faster than bone‑in but retains a high nutrient density.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken is high in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low fat (without skin)
items.content: Removing the skin reduces fat to about 3‑4 g per 100 g, fitting diets that limit fat intake.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Fat content in skin
items.content: Chicken skin is high in saturated fat; excessive consumption may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor Salmonella; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Rotisserie chicken is often marinated with salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rotisserie chicken breast can be eaten hot, sliced into salads, sandwiches, or added to pasta dishes. The skin can be left for crunch or removed to reduce fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where it keeps quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
